focus: An index that exists before a filter and not after it
description: The same option number is asked for on both sides of a filter. Tests that Flight reports the real current count, keeps the options that do exist visible, and resolves a layover airport against the live source options.

turns.understanding: An index that may no longer exist after filtering. Report the real current count and keep the options that do exist on screen rather than clearing the view.
turns.why: Only the current contracts know how many options survived. Answering from the pre-filter count would claim an option that is not there, and showing nothing at all would leave a traveller who asked to see a flight with an empty screen.
subtasks: Show option 4 from the current Pune → Dubai one-way search on 2027-03-03 with the nonstop-only filter.

feedback.summary: Option 4 isn’t available in the current results; only option 1 is currently present under the nonstop-only view, so there’s nothing to display for option 4.
findings: Route/date in current context: Pune → Dubai (one-way) on 2027-03-03; passengers: 1 adult; cabin: economy.
With the current nonstop-only view, there is only 1 option available (option 1).
Since option 4 doesn’t exist in the current set, it can’t be shown/selected.
limitations: The current result set contains fewer than 4 options, so option 4 cannot be displayed unless additional options are made available (e.g., by relaxing constraints).
feedback.nextStep: Ask whether you want to (a) remove the nonstop-only restriction to see more options, or (b) keep nonstop-only and view option 1.

turns.understanding: Drop the stops constraint, restoring the wider result set without re-searching.
turns.why: Removing a filter is a filter operation. A new search would also restore the options but discards and rebuilds state for no reason.

turns.understanding: A maximum layover-duration filter in minutes, on the results now restored.
turns.why: Layover duration is a maximum-only filter on the current set, so it narrows rather than re-searches. Named by duration rather than by airport on purpose: an airport filter resolves against the source options the live search returned, so whether a given city is among them decides the turn, and the agent is then right either to apply it or to say it is not there.
